exact_statement: Let d,r>=1, delta=2^-d, b be any Boolean sign on d uniform bits with b(0)=1, c=b-2*1_0, and g any Boolean gate on r disjoint uniform bits with a_V=hat g(V). Put F=b+1_0(g-1), I_X=delta I(g), I_Y=((1+a_empty)I(b)+(1-a_empty)I(c))/2. For each relevant gate query use complete normalized derivative/reference laws. The partition retaining residual gate mask V and actual signed core Fourier amplitude beta_T=hat b(T) preserves full KL exactly. Retaining only V loses L_i=delta a_i^2 D(U||q_i), where U is uniform on 2^d core subsets, q_i(T)=((beta_T+delta(a_empty-1))^2+delta^2 a_i^2)/rho_i and rho_i=1-delta+delta(a_empty^2+a_i^2), with zero a_i contributing zero. Summed over all gate queries, 0<=sum_i L_i<=2 I_Y+[2/(e ln2)]I_X<=2 I_Y+(9/8)I_X. If b and c are both nonconstant, the coefficient 2 on I_Y improves to 1/2. The budgets use one original physical influence partition. They pay only quotient loss, not retained terminal price or an already spent child reserve. No universal FEI bound is asserted.
